name: The Revolutions That Remade the World
description: From Dutch rebels to the Arab Spring: how crowds, armies and ideas have overturned kings, empires and governments over four hundred years.

checkpoints.name: Crowns challenged
checkpoints.note: Dutch rebels fight Spain, an English king is tried and beheaded, and in 1688 Parliament invites a new monarch, showing that rulers can be held to account.

checkpoints.name: The age of rights
checkpoints.note: American colonists break from Britain and the French overthrow their king. In Haiti, enslaved people win their freedom and found a state.

checkpoints.name: Nations against empires
checkpoints.note: Latin America, led by Simon Bolivar and others, and Greece break from imperial rule, Europe rises in 1848, rebellions shake India and China, and Japan's leaders transform their state.

checkpoints.name: Revolutions of a violent century
checkpoints.note: Revolutions topple the Chinese emperor, the Russian tsar and the German kaiser, while Mexico and Ireland fight for new orders. In China a civil war between Nationalists and Communists begins in 1927 and ends in a Communist victory in 1949.

checkpoints.name: Revolts of the Cold War
checkpoints.note: Cuban revolutionaries, Hungarian workers, Portuguese officers and Iranian crowds each overturn or challenge the order of their day.

checkpoints.name: People power
checkpoints.note: From Beijing to Prague, from Kyiv to Tunis, protest movements and peaceful crowds bring down governments, with results that range from freedom to new conflict.
